overall_statement: Calibrated strengths disagree across predictors: AlphaMissense 0.923 reaches PP3_Moderate (Bergquist 2025) and PolyPhen-2 0.997 reaches PP3_Supporting (Pejaver 2022), whereas REVEL 0.472, CADD-PHRED 24.5 and SIFT 0.01 fall in indeterminate gaps and give no PP3 strength. REVEL, the ClinGen-recommended tool of Pejaver 2022, is indeterminate. Choosing the highest-scoring tool after seeing all scores is post hoc; the defensible statement is 'PP3 at most Moderate (AlphaMissense only), none by REVEL', and the tools are correlated, so strengths must not be summed. The default AlphaMissense cut-off (0.564) is not itself calibrated evidence (Bergquist 2025).
acmg_combination_caveat: Even the most favourable reading (PM2 for rarity at Supporting, as downgraded by ClinGen SVI, plus PP3_Moderate) does not classify the variant: it remains a variant of uncertain significance (Likely pathogenic needs more points than this; point system from Tavtigian 2020, not re-verified here). PM2 and PP3 are weak lines of evidence. Phase (cis/trans relative to a second BUB1B variant) is unresolved, so no inference on biallelic status or disease can be drawn.
acmg_classification: Variant of uncertain significance (unchanged); phase unresolved

pejaver_method.text: Scores that satisfied the posterior probability thresholds presented in Table 1 were then deemed to provide the corresponding strengths of evidence ( Table 2 ).

bergquist_default_threshold.text: In fact, the recommended thresholds for AlphaMissense (0.564) and ESM1b (−7.5) do not meet the Supporting level of evidence for pathogenicity or benignity, based on our calibration.
